@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
+
+/// spec-6-4 — the save-to-journal bookmark affordance's own 4-state shape,
+/// rendered on a user chat bubble only (`ChatBubble`). Mirrors
+/// `SyncBadgeState`'s shape exactly (sealed, hand-rolled equality, `const
+/// factory` constructors on the base class so call sites read as
+/// `BookmarkState.idle()` rather than naming each subclass directly) —
+/// this shape is too small to justify pulling in `freezed` for it.
+sealed class BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkState();
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.idle() = BookmarkIdle;
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.saving() = BookmarkSaving;
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.saved() = BookmarkSaved;
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.error(Failure failure) = BookmarkError;
+}
+
+/// The default state — outline icon, never yet tapped (or tapped in an
+/// earlier app run and the session since reloaded — Design Notes: "no
+/// persisted bookmark flag", a stale `idle` after reload is harmless given
+/// the backend's own idempotency on `chatMessageId`).
+class BookmarkIdle extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkIdle();
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) => other is BookmarkIdle;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => (BookmarkIdle).hashCode;
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'BookmarkIdle()';
+}
+
+/// `EntriesRepository.create()` is in flight for this exact message, via
+/// `isolatedSideEffect` — a second tap while in this state is a no-op
+/// (`ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage`'s own re-entrancy guard).
+class BookmarkSaving extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkSaving();
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) => other is BookmarkSaving;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => (BookmarkSaving).hashCode;
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'BookmarkSaving()';
+}
+
+/// The `Entry` was created successfully — ochre check; tapping again is a
+/// client-side no-op (Boundaries), the backend's own idempotency on
+/// `chatMessageId` makes a duplicate call harmless regardless.
+class BookmarkSaved extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkSaved();
+
+  @override

+import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
+
+import 'package:cerne/core/failure/failure.dart';
+import 'package:cerne/core/isolated_side_effect.dart';
+
+/// spec-6-4 (RF10) — the first real test of `isolatedSideEffect` (AD-13):
+/// a typed stub until this story, now exercised against its two possible
+/// outcomes — [action] resolving normally, and [action] throwing, which
+/// must never propagate to the caller (RNF09).
+void main() {
+  group('isolatedSideEffect', () {
+    test(
+      'a successful action passes its value through as Right',
+      () async {
+        final result = await isolatedSideEffect<int>(() async => 42);
+
+        expect(result.isRight(), isTrue);
+        result.match(
+          (_) => fail('expected Right'),
+          (value) => expect(value, 42),
+        );
+      },
+    );
+
+    test(
+      'an action that throws synchronously is caught and mapped to '
+      'Left(Failure.malformedResponse), never propagating to the caller',
+      () async {
+        final result = await isolatedSideEffect<int>(() {
+          throw Exception('boom');
+        });
+
+        expect(result.isLeft(), isTrue);
+        result.match(
+          (failure) {
+            expect(failure, isA<MalformedResponse>());
+            expect(failure.message, contains('boom'));
+          },
+          (_) => fail('expected Left'),
+        );
+      },
+    );
+
+    test(
+      'an action whose returned Future completes with an error is caught '
+      'and mapped to Left(Failure.malformedResponse) the same way',
+      () async {
+        final result = await isolatedSideEffect<int>(
+          () async => Future.error(Exception('async boom')),
+        );
+
+        expect(result.isLeft(), isTrue);
+        result.match(
+          (failure) {
+            expect(failure, isA<MalformedResponse>());
+            expect(failure.message, contains('async boom'));
+          },
+          (_) => fail('expected Left'),
+        );
+      },
+    );
+  });
+}

  - `lib/core/isolated_side_effect.dart`'s new real implementation does `catch (error) { return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString())); }` — it discards the stack trace entirely and performs no logging of any kind.   - `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`: `chatBookmarkIconSize` is defined as a bare alias (`= entriesSearchBarIconSize`) of an unrelated token. The two values coincide at 16px per the prototype only by chance (a search-bar icon and a chat bookmark icon are unrelated design decisions); aliasing them means a future unrelated change to the search bar icon size would silently resize the chat bookmark icon too.
  - `test/main_test.dart` resolves `ChatCubit`'s new `EntriesRepository` dependency from the real DI container (`sl<EntriesRepository>()`, backed by the real `ApiClient`/`Dio`) instead of a throwing fake, breaking the pattern every other touched test file in this diff follows (a `_FakeEntriesRepository`/`_UnusedEntriesRepository` whose methods all `throw UnimplementedError('not expected to be called')`).   - `test/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker_test.dart`: the added `String? chatMessageId,` parameter line is indented with 2 spaces instead of the surrounding 4-space indentation used by `int? mediaDurationSeconds,` right above it — a `dart format` cleanup was missed.

</agent-message>

content.text: This review surfaced a real architectural violation I need to flag before going further. Let me verify one detail about the existing shared-write mechanism before presenting it to you.

The review surfaced a real, confirmed problem before I get to the smaller findings: the implementation violates an explicit project rule.

## Confirmed: RNF06/RF10 violation

**AGENTS.md** states explicitly: *"RF10 (save chat message as entry) must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly — doing so also violates RNF06."*

The implementation has `ChatCubit` and `chat_injection.dart` import `EntriesRepository` directly from `entries/domain/repositories/` and call `.create()` on it. That's exactly what the rule forbids — I missed this when writing the spec: my own frozen Boundaries text ("`ChatCubit` depends on `EntriesRepository` from `entries/domain/repositories/` only") mandated the violating design, following `epic-6-context.md`'s looser phrasing ("consumes the abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only") instead of AGENTS.md's stricter, RF10-specific rule. Since the root cause is inside the frozen intent I had you approve, this is an **intent_gap** — it needs to go back to you, not get silently patched.

I checked whether the existing `PendingEntryWriteTracker` (used by the text/audio/photo capture cubits) is the right shared seam to reuse. It isn't a clean fit: its `create()` unconditionally clears *any* existing failed pending-write record app-wide on each call (`_pending.removeWhere(status is Failed)`), written under the assumption that exactly one capture flow is ever in flight at once. Routing chat's bookmark through it risks silently clearing an unrelated capture-flow's visible error card on Meus Registros if both happen to be pending at the same time.

My recommendation: introduce a small new use-case type in `entries/domain/` (e.g. `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`, wrapping `EntriesRepository.create()` with no other behavior) and have `ChatCubit` depend on that instead. Minimal blast radius — the `chatMessageId` threading through `entries/data`/`entries/domain` stays as-is; only `ChatCubit`'s one dependency type changes, then `chat_cubit.dart`/`chat_injection.dart`/`chat_bubble.dart` get re-derived against the amended spec.

(Other reviewers also found: no test exercises the actual `chat_screen.dart` wiring end-to-end; `bookmarkMessage`'s first `emit()` lacks the `isClosed` guard its second one has; a Reduce-Motion label isn't width-constrained; and a couple of minor/cosmetic items. I'll fold those into the re-derivation regardless of which option you pick below.)

## Spec Change Log

- **Round 1 review finding (intent_gap):** The original frozen Boundaries said "`ChatCubit` depends on `EntriesRepository` from `entries/domain/repositories/` only" — implemented faithfully, but that directly violates AGENTS.md's explicit RF10 rule ("must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly — doing so also violates RNF06"). Root cause was inside the frozen block, so this is an intent_gap, not a patch.
  **Amended:** `ChatCubit` now depends on a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) instead of `EntriesRepository` directly; `EntriesRepository`/`entries/data`/`entries/presentation` imports from `chat/` are now explicitly forbidden in Boundaries.
  **Known-bad state avoided:** a cross-feature import the project's own instructions name by story number (RF10) as forbidden, which would also have made every future review of this story flag the same violation.
  **Also folded in** (surfaced by the same review round, cheap to fix alongside the use-case change since the touched files are being re-derived anyway): both `bookmarkMessage()` emits now need an `isClosed` guard, not just the second one; the Reduce-Motion label needs a width-capped slot; `chatBookmarkIconSize` should be its own literal, not an alias of an unrelated token; `chat_screen_test.dart` needs a real end-to-end tap test for the `onBookmark` wiring (previously only `ChatBubble`/`ChatCubit` were tested in isolation); `test/main_test.dart` should use a throwing fake like every other touched test file, not the real DI-resolved dependency; the `pending_entry_write_tracker_test.dart` fake's new param line had a stray 2-space indent.
  **KEEP (verified correct, must survive re-derivation):** the `BookmarkState` sealed-class shape and its placement in `chat/domain/entities/`; `ChatUiMessage.bookmarkState`'s default-idle/`copyWith` extension; the `chatMessageId` threading through `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` → `data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` → `data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` (unaffected by this amendment — the use case sits *above* this, not instead of it); `isolatedSideEffect`'s real catch-to-`malformedResponse` body; `bookmarkMessage()`'s guard chain (role/serverId/already-saved/already-saving) and its `Either`-flattening from `isolatedSideEffect`; the `ChatBubble` icon/color-per-state mapping and 44pt tap target; every I/O-matrix-covering test case already written for `chat_cubit_test.dart`/`chat_bubble_test.dart` (only their `EntriesRepository` fake swaps for a `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` fake — the test *logic* is unchanged).

## Design Notes

- `BookmarkState` lives in `chat/domain/entities/`, mirroring `SyncBadgeState`'s per-feature placement — promote only if a second feature needs it.
- `chatMessageId` sent is `ChatUiMessage.serverId`, never the local UI `id` — same distinction story 6.3 established for `retryMessage`.
- No persisted bookmark flag: reload-then-re-tap is harmless given backend idempotency — simpler than threading a new field through the Hive message cache for no behavioral gain.
- `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` is deliberately narrower than `EntriesRepository.create()` (just `content`/`chatMessageId`, `source` is implicit) — it exists only to satisfy AGENTS.md's RF10 boundary, not to become a general-purpose entries port; a future caller needing more of `create()`'s surface gets its own use case rather than this one growing extra optional params.

- A save failure never freezes the session: only the tapped bubble's state flips to `error` (retryable); composer/history/other bubbles unaffected.

Row(...) : timeCaption` ternary right below.   - **`bookmarkMessage`'s retry-on-error guard never consults `Failure.retryable`**, unlike every other failure-surfacing affordance in this codebase. `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/sync_badge.dart` and `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart` both explicitly gate "tap to retry" on `failure.retryable` (AD-3/AD-4), and `test/core/isolated_side_effect_test.dart` itself asserts a mapped `malformedResponse` is `retryable == false`. No layout/golden test catches this height change.

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-2-multi-session-chat-history-new-conversation.md`
  summary: `ChatScreen._recordScrollOffset`'s scroll listener has no awareness of an in-progress session transition — during the frame that rebuilds the list for a newly switched-to session (before `_jumpToOffset`'s post-frame callback runs), an automatic scroll-position clamp can fire this listener and record a transient, incorrect offset under the new session's id.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Self-corrects moments later once `_jumpToOffset` runs; untested latent fragility, no observed visual glitch.

## Deferred from: code review of story-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock (2026-11-06)

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: Two new `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>`s — `AppDrawer`'s "Novo Chat" disable and `ChatScreen`'s offline banner — have no `buildWhen`, so both rebuild on every `ChatReady` emission, including once per streamed AI token, even though each only cares about one boolean.
  evidence: `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter + verification-gap layers). Same unthrottled-rebuild class already deferred twice before — `ChatScreen._scrollToBottomSoon` (story 6.1) and the drawer's own "CONVERSAS" `BlocBuilder` (story 6.2) — now a third/fourth instance in the same screens.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: `ChatCubit.retryMessage()`'s no-`serverId` fallback (the stream dropped before `message_created` ever arrived) silently resends via `sendMessage`, which mints a genuinely new `chat-messages-send` call server-side — but the UI gives no indication that "retry" quietly sent a new message rather than regenerating the original one.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` (`retryMessage`). Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Explicitly sanctioned by the spec's own Boundaries/Never section as the intended fallback behavior; no acceptance criterion or Design Note calls for a distinguishing UI treatment, and introducing new user-facing copy wasn't authorized by the spec.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: `ChatReady.isOffline` defaults to `false` until `ConnectivityWatcher`'s first reading arrives; if `ChatCubit._bootstrap()` resolves first, the very first emitted `ChatReady` can briefly show the composer enabled on a device that's actually offline at launch, correcting itself only once the real reading lands.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). `chat_cubit_test.dart` already covers the opposite race ("a connectivity reading that arrives before bootstrap resolves") but not this direction; self-corrects moments later, no observed glitch — same latent-race pattern already deferred for `ChatScreen._recordScrollOffset` above.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: The new offline banner only renders while `state is ChatReady`; `ChatBootstrapLoading`/`ChatBootstrapError` never surface the offline cue even when `ChatCubit._isOffline` is already known `true` at that point.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`. Review finding (edge-case-hunter layer). Brief, self-correcting window (bootstrap normally resolves quickly); no acceptance criterion scopes the bootstrap states' offline treatment.

## Deferred from: code review of story-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock, round 2 (2026-11-06)

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: `ConnectivityPlusWatcher` reports whether a network interface is up, not whether the device has real internet reachability — a device joined to a dead Wi-Fi or captive portal is reported "online," so the composer stays enabled while a send on it still fails as `Failure.networkOffline`.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Mitigated in practice by this same story's own tap-to-retry/failed-bubble affordance — the send still fails gracefully, it's just not pre-empted by the banner. Reconciling the two independent "offline" signals would mean touching `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s existing `networkOffline` handling, which this story's Boundaries explicitly forbid ("isOffline is additive only").
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: No test covers a flapping connectivity signal — rapid true/false/true emissions, or a transition arriving mid-send/mid-retry — verifying the banner, composer, and `_isSending` state stay consistent through it.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Expected behavior for this case is unspecified anywhere in the spec's I/O matrix or Boundaries; no observed defect, just untested.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-3-dropped-stream-resilience-offline-composer-lock.md`
  summary: A successful `retryMessage` never writes the regenerated content back to the local Hive cache — if the app is force-closed right after a successful retry and relaunched offline, the cached copy of that message still shows its stale/failed content.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart` (`retryMessage`). Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Mirrors `sendMessage`'s own pre-existing "pure passthrough, no Hive persistence" design from story 6.1 — not a new asymmetry introduced by this story.

## Deferred from: code review of story-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry, round 2 (2026-11-06)

- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: `ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage`'s retry-on-error path never checks `Failure.retryable` before re-attempting — unlike `SyncBadge`/`PendingEntryWriteTracker`'s established "only a retryable failure is tappable to retry" convention (AD-3/AD-4) — so a deterministically non-retryable failure (e.g. `payloadTooLarge`) can be retried forever, always failing the same way.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` (`bookmarkMessage`). Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Deliberately not treated as a blocking defect this round: the story's own AC reads "the button resets to a retryable state rather than freezing," which plausibly means "the user is never stuck," and gating on `retryable` the way `SyncBadge` does would make a `malformedResponse` (thrown-exception) failure permanently un-retryable too — a worse outcome for that specific I/O-matrix row. Needs a deliberate human decision, not a mechanical fix.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: No UI surface explains *why* a bookmark save failed — `BookmarkError.failure` is stored on `ChatUiMessage.bookmarkState` but never read by `ChatBubble`, unlike `SyncBadge`'s inline failure-explanation expansion for a non-retryable error.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_state.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Consistent with this story's own Boundaries, which scoped the bookmark button to icon+color only, not message detail — a possible follow-up, not a defect against the stated scope.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: No accessibility live-announcement (`SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement`) fires when a bookmark save resolves to `saved`/`error` — several other async actions in the app (`InsertionModal`, `AccountSettingsScreen`, `VaultLockScreen`) do announce their own outcome, so a screen-reader user not actively touching the icon when the result lands has no way to learn it.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Not required by this story's Boundaries (icon + `Semantics.label` per state already satisfies the project's adopted "color alone never carries state" floor) — a stricter ask than what was scoped.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: A newly bookmarked Entry never appears live in an already-open "Meus Registros"/search screen — `MeusRegistrosCubit`/`EntriesSearchCubit` only learn of new entries via `PendingEntryWriteTracker`'s `confirmedWrites` stream, and this story's round-1 review explicitly chose not to route the bookmark save through that tracker (its global failed-write-clearing behavior was a poor fit for a second concurrent caller).
  evidence: `lib/features/entries/domain/usecases/save_chat_message_as_entry_use_case.dart`, `lib/features/entries/domain/services/pending_entry_write_tracker.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer), consciously accepted trade-off from this story's own intent-gap loopback (see its Spec Change Log). Not required by Story 6.4's Acceptance Criteria; a candidate for a future story if live-update parity with the capture flows turns out to matter.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: `isolatedSideEffect`'s awaited `action()` has no timeout of its own — a hung underlying network call keeps a bookmark button stuck on `saving` indefinitely, with the per-message re-entrancy guard blocking any retry until it resolves.
  evidence: `lib/core/isolated_side_effect.dart`. Review finding (edge-case-hunter layer). Pre-existing characteristic of `ApiClient`/`Dio`'s own configured timeouts, affecting every API call in the app — not introduced by, or specific to, this story.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: `EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` calls the remote data source first, then writes to the local Hive `entries` box — if that local `put()` throws, it returns `Left(malformedResponse)` even though the Entry was already durably created on the backend, so a bookmark save can show `error` (inviting a retry) for a save that actually already succeeded.
  evidence: `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` (`create`). Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Pre-existing behavior inherited from earlier entries stories (spec-3-1 onward), surfaced incidentally by this story's own review, not introduced by it.
- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`
  summary: The bookmark icon's 44pt minimum tap target inflates a user bubble's caption row height versus an AI bubble's (whose row is just the short `timeCaption` alone), a visible proportion difference no golden/layout test catches.
  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`. Review finding (blind-hunter layer). A direct, likely-unavoidable consequence of this story's own frozen Boundaries ("Tap target ≥44pt"); a visual-polish question for product/design, not a functional defect.

## Story 6.4 — Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry: complete

Opened in VS Code — the spec at [spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md](_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md) contains a **Suggested Review Order**; Cmd+click the links to jump to each stop.

**What shipped:** a four-state (idle/saving/saved/error) bookmark affordance on user chat messages, saving them as journal Entries through a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` — a shared entries-domain port that keeps `ChatCubit` from importing `EntriesRepository` directly, satisfying AGENTS.md's RF10 layering rule. Also implements the real `isolatedSideEffect` helper (previously a stub) and threads `chatMessageId` through the entries repository/data-source layers.
